summary:
ASTROTWIN is an interactive web-based astronaut health simulation platform designed to explore the challenges of maintaining crew health during long-duration space missions to the Moon and Mars. Its futuristic holographic interface displays key health indicators, including bone density, muscle mass, cardiac output, stress, and radiation exposure.

The core feature is a bio-modulation simulator based on NASA medical research. Users can adjust countermeasures such as exercise (ARED), sleep, and nutrition (Vitamin D, calcium, and protein) to forecast changes in astronaut health. The model also accounts for different gravitational environments: the ISS, the Moon, and Mars.

ASTROTWIN features a two-channel prediction system, comparing a baseline forecast with a personalized one that gradually adapts through an algorithm. It also provides diagnostic alerts, countermeasure recommendations, mission reports, and a gamified daily activity system.

By combining biological data, mathematical modelling, and AI-assisted development, ASTROTWIN explores how digital tools could help protect astronaut health during future long-duration space missions.
details:
1. How It Works

ASTROTWIN is an interactive astronaut health simulation platform designed to explore the potential effects of long-duration spaceflight on human physiology.

The system displays ten health-related indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, ocular pressure, cognitive reaction time, bone mineral density, muscle mass, cardiac output, cumulative radiation dose, physiological stress, and nutrition status.

Users can switch between three simulated environments: the International Space Station (ISS), the Moon, and Mars. They can also adjust different countermeasures, including exercise intensity, sleep duration, protein intake, calcium and vitamin D consumption, and other parameters.

The simulator uses a mathematical model implemented in JavaScript to calculate changes in six key health indicators over a selected period of 7–365 days.

For example, the bone mineral density model uses the following equation:

[
B_{t+1}=B_t-0.04g_bk(1-0.6A)
+0.003(C-1)+0.003(D-1)
]

Where:

  • (B_t) — current bone mineral density index;
  • (g_b) — environmental gravity factor;
  • (k) — individual response coefficient;
  • (A) — normalized resistance exercise load;
  • (C) — normalized calcium intake;
  • (D) — normalized vitamin D intake.

This equation is a simplified simulation rule: it estimates how environmental conditions and selected countermeasures influence the model's bone density indicator over time.

ASTROTWIN generates two projections: a baseline scenario and a personalized scenario. Users can compare the results, examine projected changes on graphs, and receive alerts when simulated indicators cross predefined thresholds.

2. Advantages

Proactive Risk Assessment: Instead of displaying only current indicators, ASTROTWIN allows users to explore possible future changes and compare different countermeasure strategies.

Multi-Environment Simulation: The platform includes separate gravity-related parameters for the ISS, Moon, and Mars, allowing users to examine how different environments affect the simulation.

Two-Channel Projection System: The simulator compares a baseline projection with a personalized projection. This makes it possible to explore how individual response assumptions can change predicted outcomes.

Interactive Countermeasures: Users can adjust exercise, nutrition, sleep, and other parameters and immediately examine their effects on the projected results.

3. Expected Effect

ASTROTWIN aims to demonstrate how mathematical modelling and interactive simulations could support astronaut health planning during long-duration missions.

The project focuses on several important physiological areas, including bone density loss, muscle atrophy, cardiovascular deconditioning, radiation exposure, and physiological stress.

In the future, the platform could be expanded by incorporating validated physiological datasets, more advanced prediction methods, and real measurements from appropriate monitoring devices.

4. Tools and Technologies

  • HTML: Application structure and interface elements.
  • CSS: Visual design, layout, animations, and responsive interface styling.
  • JavaScript: Interactive functionality, simulation logic, calculations, and data visualization.
  • SVG: Scalable holographic astronaut visualization.
  • HTML Canvas API: Telemetry graphs, ECG-style visualization, and background effects.

The current version is a standalone front-end application. Its mathematical model and simulation logic run directly in the browser.

5. Creativity and AI Integration

Algorithmic Personalization: ASTROTWIN includes a mechanism for comparing standard and individualized simulation scenarios. A predefined individual response coefficient modifies the rate of simulated physiological changes.

Calibration Mechanism: The simulator includes a confidence indicator that increases during simulated mission time. The personalization coefficient is gradually adjusted according to the programmed calibration logic. This is a scripted prototype mechanism, not a machine-learning model trained on real astronaut data.

AI-Assisted Development: AI tools were used as development assistants during the creation of the mathematical model and parts of the software. The team integrated the resulting work into the application and developed the project collaboratively.

Interactive Mission Interface: The platform combines a holographic astronaut visualization, telemetry indicators, diagnostic alerts, graphs, and a mission-style progress system to make complex simulation results easier to explore.

6. Key Factors and Project Limitations

The simulation focuses on six main model outputs:

  • Bone mineral density.
  • Skeletal muscle mass.
  • Cardiac output.
  • Cumulative radiation dose.
  • Physiological stress.
  • Nutrition score.

The model incorporates simplified environmental gravity factors and countermeasure parameters to demonstrate how different conditions and intervention strategies can influence projected health indicators.

The interface distinguishes between baseline and personalized projections using separate graph lines, allowing users to compare the two scenarios over time.

Important limitation: ASTROTWIN is an educational and research-oriented prototype, not a clinically validated medical tool. Its physiological equations and coefficients are simplified assumptions and require validation against reliable scientific data before the system could be used for real astronaut health assessment or operational decision-making. Most displayed telemetry is simulated rather than obtained from actual medical sensors.
